transcript: So number one, we are doing this interview right in the middle of August. And one of the key questions I get in my office is certainty in terms of kids being able to safely go to school. And overwhelmingly, parents in my district want to see some form, some significant form of in-person learning. Part of that is providing funds, K through 12 funds that are sorely needed in school districts because they are updating their operations. They've worked really hard to put forth safe plans for the students, they're safe for the teachers and staff. But there's an increased cost to that. So I think that's going to be important. In addition, as I've talked to small businesses, particularly from sectors that are extremely hurting right now, such as restaurants, hospitality, retail, tourism, I think they should be eligible to apply for a second round of the paycheck protection program. That has been very, very successful in my district. Small businesses have benefited from $250 million of infusion of capital, frankly, to small businesses to allow them to keep people employed. But for those sectors that are impacted, I want them to be eligible to go back a second time. In addition, in my district, I talked a little bit about the northern border trade issues at the start of the podcast. It's important to have clarity and certainty for the reopening process of the U.S. Canadian border. And I've talked about, and there's been bipartisan calls for this with my colleague, we co-chaired the Northern border caucus. of again allowing increased flexibility for those that own property or other cases. We want to slowly but surely reopen the border so that there's certainty for the business community that's been impacted.
